title: Memory consolidation
description: Decide whether a new memory duplicates or updates a stored one

topic.description: the option text of this memory in the target question, e.g. 'M3 (primary database): the new fact is about this same subject'

note.description: optional header note, e.g. 'nearest 5 by embedding'

action.instructions: Given the NEW fact and the NEAREST STORED memories, what should the memory store do with the new fact?

criteria.add: The new fact carries information not already stored (new topic, or extra detail that does not contradict anything); store it as a new memory
criteria.duplicate: An existing memory already says the same thing; drop the new fact
criteria.supersede: The new fact contradicts or updates an existing memory (a value changed); replace the old memory

target.instructions: Which stored memory does the NEW fact overlap with or update? Choose none if no stored memory is about the same subject.

extra.none: no stored memory is about the same subject

combine: duplicate if action == 'duplicate' and action.p >= act_p; supersede if action == 'supersede' and action.p >= act_p; add otherwise
limitations: only sees the state: the duplicate must be in the retriever's top-k
target is only meaningful for duplicate and supersede; below act_p the decision is add (read action_p to flag it)
zero neighbours is add without a call in the spec; here the engine refuses a one-option question, so the run degrades to add (OJ_INVALID_INPUT, no request): check for an empty list first
notes: # deviation: spec 5.19: each neighbour needs a `topic` (used verbatim as its target option text; the engine cannot derive it); zero neighbours degrades to add instead of a clean add; variant_of entity_match
